The Dark Tower - Book 1 The Gunslinger - by Stephen King

I'm just commenting here as when I tried to track down audiobooks of the Dark Tower series, I had a hard time finding information on what was available.

Just a heads-up, this link is a reading of the "revised" version; after several of the other books in the Dark Tower series had been released (and something like 20 years after the original release of The Gunslinger), King went back and made some changes/additions and re-released it, mostly in an attempt to make it more congruent with the newer books in the series. The Gunslinger is the only book in the series that got this treatment.

It's very much like what George Lucas did with the Star Wars Special Editions - mostly small changes, a word or sentence or two here and there; some just adding fluff, some making the language more consistent with the later books, and some for continuity/foreshadowing for later in the series; but most fans who experienced the original before the "special edition" existed (like myself), will always prefer the original. I don't want to post any spoilers, but some of the changes also seemed to be geared towards making some characters more likable (much like how Lucas made Greedo shoot first in his Special Editions so Han fit more of the "hero" archetype).

I don't want to come off as a book snob or "I read this before it was cool" hipster; Revised Gunslinger is better than no Gunslinger if that's what you've got access to (and it is much more readily available). But personally, given the two, I like the original better, for reasons I could discuss at length (even without spoilers). My recommendation? If you can, read the original first, then continue the series. If you can track down the Frank Muller reading, the next few books in the series were also read by him, so you also get that consistency if you continue on into the next books. If you make it through the whole series (it's pretty long), then you probably like the stories enough to revisit the Revised Gunslinger after finishing off the series, which is something I'd highly recommend doing.

King himself also recorded a reading of the original Gunslinger, but I really like the Frank Muller reading. I can't find the whole thing on YouTube, but here's "part one": https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=kekAekgbcTE

So I shared a recipe for making rice on the stove top with a work friend that I thought was 100% fail-proof. He didn't care for how his turned out. I've made this once a week for months now and I use it with a crock pot roast for what I think is a sublime dish that makes up the bulk of my daily meals.

The rice is simple. Ten cups water brought to a boil, then add five cups white jasmine rice, cover, bring back up to a boil and lower the temperature to a simmer and let cook for fifteen minutes. Remove from heat and let sit for five.

Easy, right? Well my friend told me that he thought his came out overcooked. He said it wasn't watery but it was really mushy. I couldn't give him an answer and I was hoping someone else could diagnose the problem there. He said that he didn't remove the lid until after the five minute rest time and isn't sure what went wrong either. I'd like to be able to give him something just because I've been talking up my beef and rice for awhile and I feel a bit like a failed cook here. Thanks for reading.
Question about making rice on the stove top.

Was he using Jasmine rice, or something like Uncle Ben's white rice? Different types of rice can require different amounts of water, depending on how much of the rice shell was polished off during processing. Different strands of rice can require different amounts of water and thus time, also (American wild rice takes a lot longer, for example).
From my understanding yes, he was using white jasmine rice.
I always use more water, and check on the rice while preparing the main course, when its ready I just remove the water. Never did like measuring water :)
